rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Method, Tables 2-7 - laboratory hydraulic tests of lateral samples from 14 farms in Canakkale (unused, 1-, 2-, 3-year emitters) at six pressures, plus chemical analysis of seven irrigation water sources.
rows.notes: The study reports its own data, but only on emitter clogging of plain drip laterals in farm use (15.6% of 3-year emitters fully clogged at 100 kPa; Cv, Us, Eu, Cu degrading with years of use), attributed to Ca/Mg precipitation, sediment from inadequate filtration and operation at low pressure (40-70 kPa). It does not involve fertigation at all, so it offers no evidence on fertigation-induced risks (contamination, nutrient deficit, hypoxia, wetting-front salt accumulation), and it measures nothing about soil health, the function coded for the claim. The only overlap with the passage is the word 'dripper clogging', but the study's clogging is water-quality/operational, not fertilizer-related. Treated as a technology mismatch (plain drip without fertigation cited for drip fertigation risks).

notes: Full text appears complete. Short laboratory/survey paper; no soil, crop or fertigation measurements; dispersion reported only as standard error for the discharge exponent x (Table 6) and Cv values, which concern emitter hydraulics, not the claimed soil-health effect.
